competitors.description:
BREAKING: $FRNT going live on Hedera is bigger than a normal stablecoin launch.
It is the first U.S. state-issued stable token now running on Hedera, backed by an institutional stack that includes Kraken, Fireblocks, and LayerZero.

According to @hedera, FRNT was minted on the Hedera EVM and announced during the Wyoming Stable Token Commission’s monthly meeting.
That matters because this is not a random ecosystem token. It comes from a public-sector issuer under Wyoming’s stable token framework.  

Hedera describes FRNT as designed for faster, more efficient value transfer while preserving the transparency and accountability expected of a public-sector issued asset.
That puts the emphasis on payments infrastructure, not speculation.  

This is where the launch becomes strategically interesting.
As stablecoins move closer to real-world adoption, the winning infrastructure is unlikely to be the loudest chain.
It will be the one that can support regulated issuers, financial institutions, and payment providers at scale.  

Hedera is clearly trying to position itself for exactly that role.
In the announcement, Hedera highlights consistent performance, low and predictable fees, and enterprise-grade security as reasons it fits payments use cases.  

The institutional stack around FRNT also stands out.
Hedera says FRNT is available on @krakenfx, Fireblocks underpins issuance and operations, and @LayerZero_Labs supports cross-chain interoperability.
That is a serious infrastructure setup, not a lightweight experiment.  

Another important detail is interoperability.
Hedera says users can purchase FRNT on supported networks and transfer it to other blockchains through Stargate.
That fits the broader direction of finance becoming more connected, not more siloed.  

Wyoming’s role here matters too.
According to the Hedera post, the Wyoming Stable Token Commission was established in 2023, and FRNT launched on January 7, 2026 as the first fiat-backed, fully reserved stable token issued by a public entity in the United States.  

So the bigger signal is not just a stablecoin launched on Hedera.
The bigger signal is that state-issued, fully reserved digital dollars are starting to plug into institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure.  

The real story is not just FRNT.
It is that regulated, public-sector digital dollars are starting to move onto infrastructure built for real payments, interoperability, and institutional trust.  

👉🏻 https://t.co/zxGOOdObzJ

industry.description:
Its hard to build without stable dependencies.

Something we never talked about, was the huge progress we had in our product of bring private custody, and cross-chain swaps with Polaris, with (what I consider) the most secure MPC wallet thats been built.

It worked. I'm incredibly proud of it.

MPC custody owned by your existing wallet, that would require TEE's + MPC assumptions to break in order to risk any fund loss. 0 way to centrally steal funds. Your funds at rest are private on Namada, and Polaris could execute cross-chain swaps across Cosmos, Solana, Ethereum, and route you back.

But we kept running into dependency failure after failure. Namada wouldn't upgrade to give permissionless assets for months.

Bridges repeatedly kept shutting down, refused to do their previously committed growth plans, and kept renegotiating for increasingly extractive terms. The commercials and stability to build was gone.

The prior stable players were gone. They got
- kicked out behind closed doors
- moved on due to disappointment in the ecosystem direction.
- changed to bet on EVM, then got rugged
- still bet on EVM, then got drained in a security bug

When @aaronxkong  says being on the cosmos hub gives more leverage, giving a clear stability in brand is a huge part of it. All these dependency risk problems get far better, as they used to be.

Now "enterprise strategies" has a legible story for value accrual, this makes the hub a more believable counterparty. All competitors (with existing distribution) in enterprise accrue the value privately, or are actively transitioning to do so. (https://t.co/2IjBGo1fv4) Cosmos must show how this can accrue to the token.

But even more importantly to me, this merge enables stable Cosmos DeFi. 

DEX + permissionless cosmwasm atomically. 

Its more exciting to build here, and you can do so with stable dependencies. Osmosis itself is stable, but an ecosystem needs to collectively grow together. Cosmos DeFi, always betting on maximal decentralization and cypherpunk values, will be far easier for everyone.
